### 3D Formats

Please avoid saving to STL files! They are lossy and inefficient - when saving a manifold mesh to STL there is no guarantee that the re-imported mesh will still be manifold, as the topology is lost. Please consider using [3MF](https://3mf.io/) instead, as this format was designed from the beginning for manifold meshes representing solid objects. 

If you use vertex properties for things like interpolated normals or texture UV coordinates, [glTF](https://www.khronos.org/Gltf) is recommended, specifically using the [`EXT_mesh_manifold`](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/blob/main/extensions/2.0/Vendor/EXT_mesh_manifold/README.md) extension. This allows for the lossless and efficient transmission of manifoldness even with property boundaries. Try our [make-manifold](https://manifoldcad.org/make-manifold) page to add this extension to your existing glTF/GLB models. 

Manifold provides high precision OBJ file IO, but it is limited in functionality and is primarily to aid in testing. If you are using our npm module, we have a much more capable [gltf-io.ts](https://github.com/elalish/manifold/blob/master/bindings/wasm/manifold-cad/lib/gltf-io.ts) you can use instead. For other languages we strongly recommend using existing packages that focus on 3D file I/O, e.g. [trimesh](https://trimesh.org/) for Python, particularly when using vertex properties or materials.
Example for integrating with [Assimp](https://github.com/assimp/assimp) is in `extras/meshIO.cpp`, which is used by files such as `extras/convert_file.cpp`.

## Building

Only CMake, a C++ compiler, and Python are required to be installed and set up to build this library (it has been tested with GCC, LLVM, MSVC). However, a variety of optional dependencies can bring in more functionality, see below.

Build and test (Ubuntu or similar):
```
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/elalish/manifold.git
cd manifold
mkdir build
cd build
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON .. && make
make test
```

CMake flags (usage e.g. `-DMANIFOLD_DEBUG=ON`):
- `MANIFOLD_JSBIND=[OFF, <ON>]`: Build js binding (when using the emscripten toolchain).
- `MANIFOLD_CBIND=[<OFF>, ON]`: Build C FFI binding.
- `MANIFOLD_PYBIND=[OFF, <ON>]`: Build python binding, requires `nanobind`.
- `MANIFOLD_PAR=[<OFF>, ON]`: Enables multi-thread parallelization, requires `tbb`.
- `MANIFOLD_DEBUG=[<OFF>, ON]`: Enables exceptions, timing, verbosity, OBJ test dumps. Has almost no effect on its own, but enables further runtime parameters to dump various outputs.
- `MANIFOLD_ASSERT=[<OFF>, ON]`: Enables internal assertions. This incurs around 20% runtime overhead. Requires MANIFOLD_DEBUG to work.
- `MANIFOLD_TEST=[OFF, <ON>]`: Build unit tests, requires `GTest`.
- `TRACY_ENABLE=[<OFF>, ON]`: Enable integration with tracy profiler. 
  See profiling section below.
- `ASSIMP_ENABLE=[<OFF>, ON]`: Enable integration with assimp, which is needed for some of the utilities in `extras`.
- `MANIFOLD_STRICT=[<OFF>, ON]`: Treat compile warnings as fatal build errors.
- `MANIFOLD_NO_IOSTREAM=[<OFF>, ON]`: Strip iostream- and filesystem-using
  bits from the public API and tests; useful for freestanding/embedded
  builds (e.g., `wasm32-unknown-unknown`). Defines both
  `MANIFOLD_NO_IOSTREAM` and `MANIFOLD_NO_FILESYSTEM` as PUBLIC compile
  definitions. The test suite still builds + runs — iostream-using
  TESTs in `manifold_test`/`polygon_test`/`manifoldc_test` are gated
  out under the macro. Incompatible with `MANIFOLD_DEBUG` /
  `MANIFOLD_TIMING` (which use `std::cout` for diagnostic output).

Dependency version override:
- `MANIFOLD_USE_BUILTIN_TBB=[<OFF>, ON]`: Use builtin version of tbb.
- `MANIFOLD_USE_BUILTIN_NANOBIND=[<OFF>, ON]`: Use builtin version of nanobind.

> Note: These two options can force the build to avoid using the system
> version of the dependency. This will either use the provided source directory
> via `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_*` (see below), or fetch the source from GitHub.
> Note that the dependency will be built as static dependency to avoid dynamic
> library conflict. When the system package is unavailable, the option will be
> automatically set to true (except for tbb).

> WARNING: These packages are statically linked to the library, which may be
> unexpected for other consumers of the library. In particular, for tbb, this
> create two versions of tbb when another library also bring their own tbb,
> which may cause performance issues or crash the system.
> It is not recommended to install manifold compiled with builtin tbb, and this
> option requires explicit opt-in now.

Offline building (with missing dependencies/dependency version override):
- `MANIFOLD_DOWNLOADS=[OFF, <ON>]`: Automatically download missing dependencies.
  Need to set `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_*` if the dependency `*` is missing.
- `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_TBB`: path to tbb source (if `MANIFOLD_PAR` is enabled).
- `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_NANOBIND`: path to nanobind source (if `MANIFOLD_PYBIND` is enabled).
- `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_GOOGLETEST`: path to googletest source (if `MANIFOLD_TEST` is enabled).

> Note: When `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_*` is set, CMake will use the provided
> source directly without downloading regardless of the value of
> `MANIFOLD_DOWNLOADS`.

The build instructions used by our CI are in [manifold.yml](https://github.com/elalish/manifold/blob/master/.github/workflows/manifold.yml), which is a good source to check if something goes wrong and for instructions specific to other platforms, like Windows.

summary_text:
While build, inspect properties / C API docs. But let's focus algorithm.

### Quality metric

For a triangle with vertices a,b,c:
- Edge lengths squared l0=|b-c|^2 opposite a, l1=|c-a|^2, l2=|a-b|^2.
- Area2 = |cross(b-a,c-a)|.
- Quality `q = 4*sqrt(3)*Area / (l0+l1+l2)` = ratio to equilateral (1 best, 0 degenerate). Equivalent `24*Area2 / (sqrt(3)*(l0+l1+l2)^2)`? Let's derive: Area = |cross|/2. q = 4√3 Area / sum l = 2√3 |cross| / sum l. Range 0..1. Alternatively min angle. For flips, compare minimum angle. Delaunay criterion maximizes min angle for convex quad. We can compute exact `minAngle` using atan2 or edge dot products. Avoid trig per edge? Could use `q` as metric, simpler and robust.
- For each pair of triangles sharing edge, calculate current min quality of the two; candidate after flip. Need gather 4 vertices and check convexity, new diagonal length > 0, new triangles nondegenerate, and both triangles coplanar. Then compute candidate q. If candidate min quality > current min quality + eps and valid, flip.
- Edge flip may be blocked if new diagonal already exists (would create duplicate edge and SwapEdge splits topology). Ensure no existing edge between opposite verts: check orbit of new edge endpoints. We can use `IsDuplicated`? It checks another edge leaving start ends at end for given edge. We can create function to see if diagonal exists via orbit around one vertex. `ForVert` traverses from halfedge. Need find `edge` starting at one endpoint? `ForVert` expects halfedge index with start vert? Let's inspect ForVert definition.

Tests:
1. `Quality.RemoveDegenerateFacesAndShortEdges`:
   - Construct a manifold with a tiny feature? Could use a refined cube then distort a vertex? Need a manifold with short edges below tolerance and degenerate/sliver triangle. How to create via public API? Could create a cube and `Refine` then `Warp` to add a nearly-collinear vertex; but input manifold topology must remain valid. We can use MeshGL from refined cube and move one interior vertex almost onto edge. However moving a vertex may invert adjacent triangles; choose a grid face and move an interior vertex along an edge? Let's design simpler:
     - Create a cube `Manifold::Cube().Refine(2)` with each face subdivided 2x2 (triangles). Get MeshGL, identify a vertex on the top face and move it slightly toward another vertex to create a short edge but not degenerate. E.g., top face has vertices; we can use `Warp` to shrink a thin strip? `Warp` lambda maps based on position: if y? Simpler: build via `Manifold::Extrude` of polygon with a tiny notch? That's still valid and short edges.
     - For quality flip test, use a rectangular face triangulated with a bad diagonal. Could construct a MeshGL of a box where one face is split into 2 triangles with poor diagonal and evaluate improvement. But creating valid MeshGL with custom triangulation maybe easy from Cube? A cube's faces are two triangles per face, but diagonal choice fixed. We can flip one face's diagonal manually and ensure manifold. Get cube MeshGL; modify `triVerts` of one face? Need know cube face indices. Could construct a simple flattened box via `Manifold::Cube` then use `Simplify`? Better: use `Manifold::Extrude` of rectangle; output quad face triangulation may be chosen by triangulator with poor diagonal? Possibly.
     - Use `Manifold::Cube()` and inspect qmin 0.707 (right triangles) - cube face triangles are right isosceles quality 0.866? Equilateral 1, right isosceles 0.866? Actually q = 2√3*0.5 / 2 =0.866. No flip improvement.
     - Build a unit square face with a long skinny set of triangles via `Manifold::Cube({10,0.1,1})`; face triangles are still right, quality 0.866. Slivers come from boolean/refine.
     - Use `Manifold::Cube().Refine(1)` then `Warp` to perturb triangulation? Average.
   - Perhaps easiest use boolean union of two cubes at angle, which our probe shows mean quality improves. Test:
     ```
     Manifold a=Cube(...); Manifold b=...Rotate; Manifold result=a+b;
     double before = MeanQuality(result);
     Manifold improved = result.ImproveQuality(0.01);
     EXPECT_GT(MeanQuality(improved), before);
     EXPECT_EQ(improved.NumDegenerateTris(),0);
     EXPECT_NEAR(volume, ..., 1e-9);
     EXPECT_EQ(improved.Genus(), result.Genus()); // but multiple components? cube union genus 0.
     EXPECT_EQ(status, NoError);
     ```
     This checks quality improvement and volume/manifold. Tri count might reduce if short edges < .01? For cube union, only edges ≥ maybe 0.1, so no collapse. Good. qmean improved as probe. Need ensure `ImproveQuality(0.01)` actually flips (yes).
   - For short edge collapse + degenerate face removal, use twin model with tolerance e.g. 1e-2, check triangle count decreases, q10 improves, volume within maybe 0.01 relative, degenerate 0. But reading models in tests slows (20s); existing GenericTwin test runs 22s. We can use a smaller synthetic.
     - Create a thin sliver by extruding a polygon with a tiny notch? Let's think.
     - Boolean union of cube and cube offset by tiny amount (e.g., 1e-5) creates near-coincident sliver surfaces. `a + a.Translate({1e-5,0,0})` maybe result has degenerate short edges; but Boolean may already collapse them within epsilon? epsilon for unit ~1e-12, so 1e-5 > eps, leaving slivers. With `ImproveQuality(1e-3)`, should collapse. Let's test with probe.

    args = [prefix]
    for col in ("col0", "col1", "col2", "col3"):
        for row in ("x", "y", "z"):
            args.append(f"{float(transform[col][row]):f}")

def run_command(
    args: list[str], cwd: Path | None = None, log_path: Path | None = None
) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    print("+ " + " ".join(args))
    sys.stdout.flush()
    if log_path is None:
        return subprocess.run(args, check=True, cwd=cwd)

    log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    result = subprocess.run(
        args,
        check=False,
        cwd=cwd,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
    )
    output = result.stdout
    if output:
        print(output, end="")
    log_path.write_text("+ " + " ".join(args) + "\n" + output, encoding="utf-8")
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise subprocess.CalledProcessError(
            result.returncode, args, output=result.stdout

def parse_cases(raw: str) -> list[int]:
    cases = []
    for part in raw.replace(",", " ").split():
        cases.append(int(part))
    if not cases:
        raise ValueError("No weekly benchmark cases were provided")
    return cases


def transform_args(prefix: str, transform: dict) -> list[str]:
    args = [prefix]
    for col in ("col0", "col1", "col2", "col3"):
        for row in ("x", "y", "z"):
            args.append(f"{float(transform[col][row]):f}")
    return args


def run_command(
    args: list[str], cwd: Path | None = None, log_path: Path | None = None
) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    print("+ " + " ".join(args))
    sys.stdout.flush()
    if log_path is None:
        return subprocess.run(args, check=True, cwd=cwd)

    log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    result = subprocess.run(
        args,
        check=False,
        cwd=cwd,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
    )
    output = result.stdout
    if output:
        print(output, end="")
    log_path.write_text("+ " + " ".join(args) + "\n" + output, encoding="utf-8")
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise subprocess.CalledProcessError(
            result.returncode, args, output=result.stdout
        )
    return result

    ]
    if sys.platform == "darwin":

def run_ember_case(
    binary: Path, spec: dict, mesh_dir: Path, threads: int, verbose: int, cwd: Path
) -> str:
    mesh_a = get_mesh(int(spec["id_a"]), mesh_dir)
    mesh_b = get_mesh(int(spec["id_b"]), mesh_dir)
    args = [
        str(binary),
        str(mesh_a),
        str(mesh_b),
        *transform_args("-t1", spec["transform_a"]),
        *transform_args("-t2", spec["transform_b"]),
        "--threads",
        str(threads),
        "--verbose",
        str(verbose),
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(
        args, check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True, cwd=cwd,
    )
    return result.stdout


def run_ember_suite(ctx: BuildContext, binary: Path) -> None:
    out_dir = ctx.out_dir / "ember_phase"
    mesh_dir = (
        ctx.source_dir / "extras" / "ember_tests" / "testfiles" / "raw_meshes"
    )
    spec_file = (
        ctx.source_dir
        / "extras"
        / "ember_tests"
        / "testfiles"
        / "ember-benchmark-cases.json"
    )
    cases = parse_cases(os.getenv("WEEKLY_BENCHMARK_CASES", DEFAULT_EMBER_CASES))
    threads = int(os.getenv("WEEKLY_BENCHMARK_THREADS", "1"))
    verbose = int(os.getenv("WEEKLY_BENCHMARK_VERBOSE", "2"))

    specs = load_ember_specs(spec_file, cases)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    write_ember_cases_metadata(out_dir, specs)

    for run_index in range(1, ctx.repeats + 1):
        run_file = out_dir / f"run{run_index}.txt"
        benchmark_csv = out_dir / "benchmark.csv"
        benchmark_csv.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        with run_file.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as out:
            for spec in specs:
                out.write(f"### case {spec['case_index']}\n")
                stdout = run_ember_case(
                    binary.resolve(),
                    spec,
                    mesh_dir.resolve(),
                    threads,
                    verbose,
                    out_dir.resolve(),
                )
                out.write(stdout)
                if not stdout.endswith("\n"):
                    out.write("\n")

        if benchmark_csv.exists():
            benchmark_csv.replace(out_dir / f"benchmark_run{run_index}.csv")

        print(f"completed Ember benchmark run {run_index}/{ctx.repeats}")
        sys.stdout.flush()


def run_perf_size_sweep_suite(ctx: BuildContext, binary: Path) -> None:
    out_dir = ctx.out_dir / "perf_size_sweep"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    prefix = "nTri="

        if value.isdigit():

    return benchmark

def parse_gtest_run(run_path: Path, run_index: int) -> dict:
    report = json.loads(run_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    tests = []
    for testsuite in report.get("testsuites", []):
        for test in testsuite.get("testsuite", []):

+# Mesh quality cleanup
+
+Manifold's Boolean operations guarantee a valid, oriented 2-manifold and the
+correct solid volume. That contract does not imply a well-shaped triangulation:
+near-coincident input faces, tiny intersection edges, and narrow clipped regions
+can leave needles and slivers. `Manifold::ImproveQuality()` is an explicit
+post-processing pass for those cases. It does not change the result of the
+Boolean itself.
+
+## API
+
+```cpp
+Manifold improved = result.ImproveQuality(tolerance);
+Manifold improved = result.Cleanup(tolerance);  // alias
+```
+
+The same operation is exposed as:
+
+- C: `manifold_improve_quality()` and `manifold_cleanup()`
+- Python: `manifold.improve_quality()` and `manifold.cleanup()`
+- TypeScript/JavaScript: `manifold.improveQuality()` and `manifold.cleanup()`
+
+`tolerance` has units of length and defaults to the manifold's current epsilon.
+Increasing it collapses longer short edges. It is not a smoothing radius and it
+does not simplify well-shaped regions.
+
+## What the pass does
+
+1. **Removes degenerate triangles.** It reuses the same edge-collapse and
+   edge-swap machinery as Boolean cleanup.
+2. **Collapses short edges.** Edges no longer than `tolerance` are candidates
+   only when the quadric collapse error is also within `tolerance`. Collapses
+   are sorted by error and rejected if they would invert or overly distort a
+   neighboring triangle.
+3. **Improves triangle shape.** Every coplanar pair of adjacent triangles is
+   tested with the alternative diagonal. The diagonal is flipped only when it
+   raises the worse of the two triangle qualities. Quality is normalized so
+   that 1 is equilateral and 0 is degenerate:
+
+   ```text
+   q = 2 * sqrt(3) * |(b - a) x (c - a)| / (|b - a|^2 + |c - b|^2 + |a - c|^2)
+   ```
+
+4. **Restores internal invariants.** Face/vertex normals are recomputed and the
+   result is re-sorted into the usual compact Manifold layout.
+
+## Guarantees
+
+- The output is a valid oriented 2-manifold. Status is propagated from the
+  input, and a round trip through `MeshGL`/`MeshGL64` remains valid.
+- Coplanar edge flips keep exactly the same quadrilateral surface, so they do
+  not change volume or area. Only flips whose local volume change is within
+  numerical epsilon are accepted.
+- A short-edge collapse moves the surface by at most `tolerance` and is only
+  accepted when its quadric error is within `tolerance` as well.
+- Non-coplanar quads are not flipped. A sliver whose neighbors cannot form a
+  valid convex quad may therefore remain: quality improvement is best effort,
+  while manifoldness and volume preservation are hard requirements.
+- Vertex properties are carried through the existing edge-collapse and
+  edge-swap interpolation paths. Property seams are not deliberately moved.
+
+## Tests and benchmark
+
+`test/quality_test.cpp` covers:
+
+- short-edge and sliver removal on an extruded notch,
+- volume, area, genus, and manifold round-trip preservation across a Boolean,
+- quality improvement from `Simplify()`, and
+- a 30k+ triangle Boolean workload used as the benchmark signal.
+
+`Quality.ImproveQualityBenchmark` is included in the weekly benchmark suite by
+`scripts/run_weekly_benchmarks.py`, so its runtime is tracked alongside the
+existing Boolean and tessellation benchmarks.

# Mesh quality cleanup

Manifold's Boolean operations guarantee a valid, oriented 2-manifold and the
correct solid volume. That contract does not imply a well-shaped triangulation:
near-coincident input faces, tiny intersection edges, and narrow clipped regions
can leave needles and slivers. `Manifold::ImproveQuality()` is an explicit
post-processing pass for those cases. It does not change the result of the
Boolean itself.

## API

```cpp
Manifold improved = result.ImproveQuality(tolerance);
Manifold improved = result.Cleanup(tolerance);  // alias
```

The same operation is exposed as:

- C: `manifold_improve_quality()` and `manifold_cleanup()`
- Python: `manifold.improve_quality()` and `manifold.cleanup()`
- TypeScript/JavaScript: `manifold.improveQuality()` and `manifold.cleanup()`

`tolerance` has units of length and defaults to the manifold's current epsilon.
Increasing it collapses longer short edges. It is not a smoothing radius and it
does not simplify well-shaped regions.

## What the pass does

1. **Removes degenerate triangles.** It reuses the same edge-collapse and
   edge-swap machinery as Boolean cleanup.
2. **Collapses short edges.** Edges no longer than `tolerance` are candidates
   only when the quadric collapse error is also within `tolerance`. Collapses
   are sorted by error and rejected if they would invert or overly distort a
   neighboring triangle.
3. **Improves triangle shape.** Every coplanar pair of adjacent triangles is
   tested with the alternative diagonal. The diagonal is flipped only when it
   raises the worse of the two triangle qualities. Quality is normalized so
   that 1 is equilateral and 0 is degenerate:

   ```text
   q = 2 * sqrt(3) * |(b - a) x (c - a)| / (|b - a|^2 + |c - b|^2 + |a - c|^2)
   ```

4. **Restores internal invariants.** Face/vertex normals are recomputed and the
   result is re-sorted into the usual compact Manifold layout.

## Guarantees

- The output is a valid oriented 2-manifold. Status is propagated from the
  input, and a round trip through `MeshGL`/`MeshGL64` remains valid.
- Coplanar edge flips keep exactly the same quadrilateral surface, so they do
  not change volume or area. Only flips whose local volume change is within
  numerical epsilon are accepted.
- A short-edge collapse moves the surface by at most `tolerance` and is only
  accepted when its quadric error is within `tolerance` as well.
- Non-coplanar quads are not flipped. A sliver whose neighbors cannot form a
  valid convex quad may therefore remain: quality improvement is best effort,
  while manifoldness and volume preservation are hard requirements.
- Vertex properties are carried through the existing edge-collapse and
  edge-swap interpolation paths. Property seams are not deliberately moved.

## Tests and benchmark

`test/quality_test.cpp` covers:

- short-edge and sliver removal on an extruded notch,
- volume, area, genus, and manifold round-trip preservation across a Boolean,
- quality improvement from `Simplify()`, and
- a 30k+ triangle Boolean workload used as the benchmark signal.

`Quality.ImproveQualityBenchmark` is included in the weekly benchmark suite by
`scripts/run_weekly_benchmarks.py`, so its runtime is tracked alongside the
existing Boolean and tessellation benchmarks.

## Example

```cpp
#include "manifold/manifold.h"

using namespace manifold;

Manifold MakeBracket() {
  Manifold body = Manifold::Cube({40, 20, 8}, true);
  Manifold hole = Manifold::Cylinder(12, 4, 4, 64);
  Manifold result = body - hole.Rotate(90, 0, 0);

  // Clean up the clipped rim without changing the solid.
  return result.ImproveQuality(result.GetEpsilon() * 100);
}
```

Our `volumeDelta` threshold uses `16*epsilon_*maxEdge²`. Consider coplanar quadrilateral with huge coordinates and tiny edges; local differences okay. Good.

We call `Continuous(edge)` before computing, which checks `triRef` and `NumProp`; but if `meshRelation_.triRef.size()==NumTri()` yet refs are all zeros or malformed? fine.

**实现内容**
- 新增 `Manifold::ImproveQuality(tolerance)`，并提供 `Cleanup()` 与 `RemoveDegenerates(tolerance)` 兼容入口，见 `include/manifold/manifold.h:232`、`src/manifold.cpp:414`。
- `CollapseShortEdges()` 仅折叠长度和 quadric 误差都小于 `tolerance` 的边，见 `src/edge_op.cpp:152`。
- `OptimizeTriangleQuality()` 对共面相邻三角形做对角线翻转，以提升两者中较差的三角形质量；拒绝非凸四边形、重复边、属性缝和会改变局部体积的翻转，见 `src/edge_op.cpp:244`。
- `Simplify()` 和公开的 `RemoveDegenerates()` 现在也会执行质量优化；布尔运算本身保持原有显式后处理语义。
- C、Python、TypeScript/JavaScript 绑定均已暴露新接口。

**测试与基准**
- 新增 `test/quality_test.cpp`，覆盖短边/退化面折叠、三角形质量提升、流形往返、体积/面积/genus 保持、错误传播、`Simplify()` 质量改善。
- `Quality.ImproveQualityBenchmark`（30k+ 三角形布尔结果）已加入每周基准套件，见 `scripts/run_weekly_benchmarks.py:36`。
- 新增 C 绑定 smoke test：`test/manifoldc_test.cpp`。
- 验证结果：`644/644` 项 CTest 全部通过；`MANIFOLD_DEBUG=ON` + `MANIFOLD_ASSERT=ON` 下的质量与 Simplify 测试通过；Python 绑定构建及运行时 smoke test 通过。

**文档**
- 新增 `docs/MeshQuality.md`，说明算法、API、保证与限制。
- `README.md:72` 增加入口说明。

短边折叠带来的是受 `tolerance` 约束的几何变化；共面翻转保持体积。对于邻接关系无法形成有效凸四边形的长条 sliver，质量优化是尽力而为，仍优先保证流形与体积。
